what_it_does: Some storage systems pair NAND flash (the kind of chip inside a USB drive or SSD) with a hard disk drive that uses a technique called Shingled Magnetic Recording (SMR), where data tracks overlap like roof shingles to pack more data onto the disk — but rewrites become complicated. The flash acts as a fast scratch pad in front of the slower disk. The problem is that flash chips can only be written to a limited number of times before they wear out, and heavy use burns through that budget quickly. MiniWear introduces a two-tier buffer: one tier lives on the flash itself and another lives on a reserved section of the SMR disk, together spreading write traffic more evenly across both media. A scheduling layer also watches for idle periods and proactively balances wear across the storage system to extend its useful life.
